newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-10-MAN SAUDI ARABIA CLINCH THIRD ASIAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-10-MAN SAUDI ARABIA CLINCH THIRD ASIAN CUP.

text.p: A 10-man Saudi Arabia held on to a goalless draw after extra time in the Asian Cup final on Saturday and went on to clinch the title for the third time by beating hosts the United Arab Emirates 4-2 on penalties.

Playmaker Khalid Al Muwalid scored the crucial penalty to silence the majority of the 60,000-strong crowd at Abu Dhabi stadium. The fans had just watched in horror their hero Hassan Ahmed hit a spot kick against a post.
Both goalkeepers had earlier saved a penalty each.
Saudi Arabia, who won the title in 1984 and 1988 and lost in the final four years ago, have now equalled Iran's record of three wins in the competition.
They achieved victory despite having 19-year-old defender Hussain Sulaimani sent off for his second bookable offence in the 86th minute.
The Saudis defended well to keep the UAE at bay in extra time to force the shootout.
Disappointed home fans streamed out of the stadium leaving behind some 5,000 flag-waving Saudis celebrating the win and watching their heroes collecting the cup.
The hosts later cancelled the traditional post-match press conference by both coaches.

Tension in the second half of normal time in an untidy match threatened to boil over and tempers on both sides were lost as tackles flew in midfield but the Malaysian referee kept the lid on some possible nasty confrontations.
The Saudis were reduced to 10 men when Sulaimani was sent off for an intentional hand ball. He had been booked earlier in the match.
The UAE began the extra time period brightly but could not deliver the killer ball for the frontmen.
The Saudis hit back with dangerous counter attacks and UAE keeper Muhsin Fairouz produced a brilliant save from a long- range drive by Al Muwalid to keep the hosts in the match.
The game had started at a slow pace with both teams adopting cautious tactics but exchanging fierce tackles.
It took 15 minutes for the first shot on target, with UAE's keeper Fairouz comfortably saving a deflected Saudi free kick.

Five minutes later, Saudi keeper Mohammed Al Daeyea produced a superb reflex effort to deny the UAE an opener. He dived to his left to push out a free shot from 10 metres out by striker Adnan Al-Talyani.
Both teams continued to battle it out in midfield, restricting strikers on both ends of the field to try their luck from long-range with shots that often missed the target.
Talyani again came close in the 31st minute, putting a header from a corner just wide.
The Saudis had strong appeals for a penalty turned down in the 37th minute when a UAE defender appeared to have put out a hand to deflect a cross in the penalty area.
A glaring miss by Talyani three minutes into the second half denied the home team a goal.
Substitute Zuhair Bkhait dispossessed a Saudi defender on the edge of the box, took the ball to the byline and sent in a low cross to Talyani that beat the keeper.
An unmarked Talyani stabbed the ball over the bar of an empty net from two metres out to the disbelief of his teammates and the home crowd.
The UAE had more of the ball after the miss but could not create another goal scoring opportunity.
Earlier in the day, Iran beat Kuwait 3-2 in another penalty-shootout after a 1-1 draw in fulltime to clinch third spot in the championship.
Iranian strikers Ali Daei and Khodadad Azizi collected the top scorer and best player awards respectively and the team also won the fair-play award.
The Asian Football Confederation announced that Lebanon would host the 12th Asian Cup in the year 2000.
Teams:

Saudi Arabia: 1-Mohammed Al Daeyea; 2-Mohammed Al Jahani; 3- Mohammed Al Khilaiwi (12-Ibrahim Al Harbi 77); 4-Abdullah Zubrom; 8-Khalid Al Temawi; 9-Sami Al Jaber (25-Abdullah Al Dossary 62); 10-Fahad Mahalel (20-Hamzah Falatah 80); 13-Hussain Sulaimani; 14-Khalid Al Mowaled; 15-Yousif Al Thunai; 16-Khamis Al Dossary.

UAE: 17-Muhsin Fairouz; 3-Munther Abdulla; 5-Yousef Saleh; 6-Ismail Ismail; 7-Bakhit Saad (13-Abdulaziz Mohamed 46); 10- Adnan Al Talyani (14-Khamis Saad 91); 12-Hassan Mubarak; 15- Mohamed Mohamed; 16-Hassan Ahmed; 18-Ahmed Ahmed; 23-Adel Ahmed (11-Zuhair Bkhait 46).
